analysis:
The PR adds one environment variable, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS, to the launchd passthrough allowlist (LaunchAgent.swift, patch hunks near head lines 332 and 375). It also updates docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: the date, and the passthrough sentence at lines 311-316. The docs also describe the delta-checkpoint and other cache behaviour at lines 254-265, but those hunks are not in the changed ranges, so I treated them as unchanged context.

Security effect: the variable is a rollback knob. A negative value makes complete checkpoints be written whole instead of as deltas. It does not touch the keys, the AAD, the HMAC lookup tags, the TTL, the disk budget or the daily write cap. Its only effect is on write format and volume. It cannot weaken the T-041 properties: HMAC-keyed names, scope folding, the 30-minute TTL, the KEK purge and AES-GCM authentication.

Attack surface: forwarding it to the launchd job lets whoever controls the launchd environment or the plist pick the checkpoint format. That actor is the local operator, who is already inside the TB-003 trust boundary and can set much more powerful variables, including DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0. Both the kill switch and this knob are already on the allowlist. The test-root, ephemeral-key and persistent-key controls stay off the list, as the docs state, so the new entry does not widen unsafe test paths. Full-file writes still go through the same write budget; the doc at line 375 says all checkpoint writes are debited against it.

The source of SSDPrefixCachePolicy.incrementalCheckpointsFlag is not supplied, so I could not verify that the constant exists or has the documented name. A missing constant would break the build rather than create a vulnerability. The delta-chain read path (the chain-read code cited at line 264, bounds at line 262) is outside this diff.

No findings. No threat-model update is needed beyond the doc change already made.
